issues.legal_issue: A state legislature cannot impose a cess on mining royalty by treating royalty as land revenue or as a tax on land when the levy is in substance a tax on royalty and the central mineral-development regime occupies the relevant field.
material_facts: A mining lessee was required to pay royalty calculated by reference to minerals extracted under a central statutory regime.
A state law imposed a local cess calculated as a proportion of land revenue and, by an amendment, included mining royalty in the definition of land revenue.
The levy was triggered by mining activity and minerals extracted; it was not calculated by valuing the land as a unit.
The central law prescribed royalty rates and provided for their alteration by the central government.
issues.conclusion: The cess on royalty was beyond the state legislature’s competence and could not be sustained as a tax on land; the levy was declared ultra vires prospectively.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 246 and the Seventh Schedule, legislative entries are fields of legislation, and a law is classified by its pith and substance, giving the entries broad scope (Calcutta Gas Co. v. State of West Bengal; H.R. Banthia v. Union of India; Union of India v. H.S. Dhillon; D.C. Rataria v. Bhuwalka Brothers). A tax under List II Entry 49 must be directly imposed on land as a unit; a levy measured by minerals extracted is not such a tax (Raja Jagannath Baksh Singh v. State of U.P.; S.C. Nawn v. WTO; Assistant Commissioner of Urban Land Tax v. Buckingham and Carnatic Co.; New Manek Chand Spinning and Weaving Mills v. Municipal Corporation of Allahabad). Royalty is related to minerals extracted, and a cess on royalty is a tax on royalty. The regulation of mines and mineral development is subject to List I Entry 54 and List II Entries 23 and 50; the central declaration and the royalty provisions in sections 2 and 9 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, occupy the relevant field and limit state competence. H.R.S. Murthy v. Collector of Chittoor, which treated a cess calculated on royalty as a tax on land, was overruled; the Court also relied on The Hingir-Rampur Coal Co. v. State of Orissa, State of Orissa v. M.A. Tulloch & Co., and Baijnath Kedia v. State of Bihar.

rule.if: constitutional_levy_challenge and levy_measured_by_royalty and royalty_tracks_extracted_minerals and central_mineral_regime_controls_royalty

predicates.constitutional_levy_challenge: A party challenged the constitutional competence of a state legislature to impose a levy.
predicates.levy_measured_by_royalty: The state levy was calculated by reference to royalty payable by a mining lessee.
predicates.royalty_tracks_extracted_minerals: The royalty was calculated by reference to minerals extracted or consumed from the leased area.
predicates.central_mineral_regime_controls_royalty: A national legal regime controlled mineral development and prescribed or controlled the royalty payable.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns a state levy measured by royalty on extracted minerals within a nationally controlled mineral regime, the output is that the state cannot impose a cess on that royalty.

issues.legal_issue: A levy previously collected in reliance on an earlier decision upholding it may be declared invalid prospectively without requiring repayment of amounts already collected.
material_facts: A prior decision of the Supreme Court had upheld a similar levy calculated on royalty.
The state had collected the cess in reliance on that decision.
The Court held the levy invalid but limited the effect of its declaration to the future.
issues.conclusion: The levy was invalid only prospectively, and the state was not required to refund cess already paid or collected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court limited retrospective relief because amounts had been collected on the basis of H.R.S. Murthy v. Collector of Chittoor, which it was overruling. It therefore declared the levy ultra vires prospectively and denied refunds of amounts already paid or collected.

predicates.challenge_to_levy: A party challenged a levy that had already been collected.
predicates.earlier_high_court_decision_upheld_simil: The highest court had previously upheld a similar levy.
predicates.collections_made_in_reliance: The government collected the levy in reliance on the earlier decision.

issues.definition: When a challenged levy was collected in reliance on an earlier decision upholding a similar levy, the output is prospective invalidity without repayment of prior collections.
